extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs and Department of the Interior officials; Indian agents and agency administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A United States Indian agent's annual/reporting narrative covering health, education, population, agriculture, crime, infrastructure, finances, and council recommendations for a reservation during a given fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health / medical practice and mortality causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on health conditions: evidence of improvement in health, counts of births and deaths (e.g., 37 births, 24 deaths), presence and impact of venereal diseases contracted from soldiers, and hereditary/long-term ailments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include numerical vital statistics, identify prevalent diseases and their origins (e.g., venereal disease from soldiers), remark on physician activity, and assess long-term prognosis (e.g., 'It will be long years with skilled attention to eradicate this great evil'). Note how diseases affect mortality and population trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education — day-school and boarding-school operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe school staffing (principal and assistant), attendance averages, completion and capacity of boarding-school houses (e.g., accommodates 60–75 children), curriculum (English branches), and special provisions for distant children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number enrolled, average and peak daily attendance, months kept, teachers employed, boarding department operations (noonday meals, matron), and recommendations (e.g., establishing boarding/labor school for children who live far away). Include outcomes like literacy counts and transfers to other schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christian work / missionary and religious activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of preaching and religious services (preaching once each Sabbath, Sunday evening services, Tuesday class meetings, Thursday prayer meetings), singing-schools for adults and children, Sunday-school together with whites, and general religious interest or awakenings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail frequency and leadership of religious services, participation by Indians (sometimes leading services), existence of singing-schools, and assessment of interest and effectiveness ('as a whole they have scarcely met my expectations' versus later awakenings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency buildings and infrastructure improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe buildings used and completed during year: store and granary, boarding-school house (size, furnishing, location), houses built for Indians, saw-mill status (destroyed by fire), grist-mill operation, and other physical improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide condition, capacity, uses, and locations of structures; comment on utility (playgrounds, inclosures), and recommend funding or reconstruction as needed (e.g., forwarding funds to reconstruct saw-mill, note that mill-dam and flume are uninjured and some machinery reusable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Population and tribal composition
rubrics_metrics.description: List tribes and population counts (e.g., total Indians ~1,000 across Walla Walla, Cayuse, Umatilla; other agency counts: Wascoes 218, Warm Springs 215, Teninoes 76, John Days 18, Piutes 27), note mixed bloods and male/female breakdowns, and comment on self-supporting status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed tribal breakdowns, note recent movements or transfers (e.g., Piutes brought from Vancouver Barracks), state levels of self-sustenance and adoption of customs, and any changes year-over-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture — acreage, crops, and yields
rubrics_metrics.description: Report acres cultivated by Indians (e.g., 2,000 acres), quantities produced (e.g., 3,000 bu wheat, 500 bu corn, 500 bu oats, 200 bu barley, 1,000 bu potatoes, 600 tons hay), and factors affecting yield (dry/cold spring, grasshoppers/crickets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include acreage under cultivation, crop-by-crop yields and changes since last year, causes for crop failures, and expectations for future seasons. Note use of agency crops and impacts on food supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock raising — numbers and economic importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of stock owned (horses prominent: totals like ~26,000 head for some agencies, or agency-specific counts such as 3,900 horses), revenue estimates from stock raising (e.g., yearly revenue not less than $50,000), and practices (herding, vulnerability to wild animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide estimates for numbers by class (horses, cattle, sheep), discuss economic role of stock raising versus agriculture, note losses (disease, weather), and any trends (sales to drovers, butchering for food).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vital statistics — births and deaths
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide births and deaths counts and net change (e.g., excess of births over deaths giving an increase of 5; elsewhere births 21, deaths 16 giving net 5), age distribution of deaths (old and children), and causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute numbers and net population change, attribute causes where known, and highlight demographic trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian apprentices / vocational training
rubrics_metrics.description: List number and placement of Indian apprentices (e.g., six apprentices: two in grist-mill, two in saw-mill/wagon-shop, one in wagon-shop, one in blacksmith shop) and assessment of their progress ('commendable progress', blacksmith apprentice can do 'all kinds of ordinary work').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document shop placements, duties performed, skill development, supervisory arrangements, and outcomes (workmanlike ability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime, law enforcement, and prosecutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of depredations, murders, convictions (e.g., convictions for selling whisky to Indians), sentences (e.g., two years in penitentiary for horse-stealing), Indian council punishments (fines, divorces), and cooperation with U.S. district attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report criminal incidents, identify perpetrators (when known), list legal actions taken by courts and Indian councils, note role of district attorney and military, and quantify convictions where possible. Mention causes of offenses (e.g., whisky) and efforts to reduce them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council propositions regarding land, inheritance, and local governance (collective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of propositions agreed upon at council (Jan 10, 1880) to be forwarded for incorporation into agreement: extend U.S. inheritance laws; allow 5-year leases; set aside two sections for church/school; appropriate sale proceeds for manual-labor and boarding school; survey and sell town-adjacent land; receive cash payments from land sales; allow 40 acres timber-land in addition to 160 acres; retain an agent to distribute sale proceeds; and promptly survey the reservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full text or close paraphrase of each numbered proposition, the Indians' reasons for each request, and note that these were to be forwarded to the Secretary of the Interior for possible incorporation before Congressional action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 1 — extend U.S. laws of inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that the laws of inheritance of the United States be extended over all Indians taking land in severalty to secure rightful heirs to real and personal property and prevent division by custom among friends of deceased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State rationale (prevent customary informal division), and recommend formal legal extension if goal is to secure clear title for heirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 2 — allow lease privilege for five years
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to allow Indians the privilege to lease land for a term of five years to enable those unable (old, sick, etc.) to derive revenue from land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain beneficiaries (those unable to farm), the proposed lease term (five years), and expected economic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 3 — reserve land for church and school
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that two sections of land be set apart for church and school purposes to become self-supporting in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify that land set aside should support religious and educational institutions and eventually be self-sustaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 4 — appropriate sale proceeds for boarding/manual-labor school
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that sufficient money from land sale be appropriated to erect and furnish a manual-labor and boarding school for children, to board them, employ two teachers and a matron, and supply books and stationery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail budgetary needs (building, furnishings, boarding, staffing, materials), emphasize need because day-school impractical when households are scattered up to 25 miles apart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 5 — survey and sell town-adjacent land in small lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to survey land adjoining Pendleton (about 160 acres) and sell it in small quantities for building purposes so Indians derive greater benefit than by having a single Indian occupy and later dispose of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reasoning (better benefit to community when sold in small parcels), include acreage and intended land use (building).

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 6 — receive cash payments from land sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that Indians be paid in cash for monies accruing from land sales because they claim to buy and sell judiciously and prefer money to goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note preference and argument for monetary payments rather than goods; consider mechanisms for secure disbursement and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 7 — optional 40 acres of timber-land in addition to 160 acres
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that each person entitled to 160 acres be allowed an additional 40 acres of timber-land if chosen, because some agricultural land lacks timber needed for building, fencing, and fuel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe optional nature of timber allotment, and the practical justification (access to timber for construction and fuel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 8 — retain an agent to distribute sale proceeds and protect interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that an agent be retained to distribute money accruing from land sales and to guard Indians' interests against surrounding whites, as Indians fear interference and meddling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain protective role of an agent, reasons for distrust of surrounding settlers, and the administrative function of distribution oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council proposition 9 — prompt reservation survey to enable locating
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that the reservation be surveyed as soon as possible to enable Indians to locate during the coming summer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize urgency to allow Indians to build fences and locate claims (stakes of old survey decayed), and recommend immediate completion of surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency mills — saw-mill and grist-mill performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report saw-mill output (e.g., 20,000 ft vs 50,000 ft prior year), reasons for reduced output (new mill nearby, old mill repair status), grist-mill running almost continuously and run by apprentices, with mill-stones dressed and kept in fair order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include output figures, causes for change, description of operations (who runs them), and note needs for additional power or repairs. Identify economic importance of mills and plans for repair/reconstruction funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and condition of Indian houses
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of houses occupied by Indians (e.g., 87 houses, all but 7 frame), description of quality and furnishings, incidents (best house burned), and general domestic standards (neat and clean).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numbers, types (frame vs other), condition, household goods status after events (fires), and examples of living standards (table-cloths, prepared meals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furs and skins sales — counts and valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate number of furs/skins sold (e.g., over 1,000 deer skins plus other species totaling ~1,200 skins) and approximate value (e.g., not less than $350).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide species breakdown where possible, estimated counts and market valuation, and note role of fur sales in agency economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsistence sources and proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of subsistence sources: 'Fully ten-sixteenths' from labor, five-sixteenths from fishing/hunting/root-gathering, and one-sixteenth from rations issued to certain groups (Piutes, apprentices, policemen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report proportional reliance on self-labor versus traditional subsistence and rations, and discuss implications for self-sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency employees — staffing and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: List of employes (e.g., physician, clerk, sawyer, Indian miller and superintendent of farming), note vacancies and needs (teacher and assistant wanted), and assessment of performance ('performed their duties satisfactorily').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide staff roles, numbers (white and Indian employes), assessments of performance, salary recommendations, and staffing requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing/adoption of citizens' dress
rubrics_metrics.description: Report number who wear citizens' dress (e.g., 479 out of 558), noting exceptions mainly among children; observation that Indians over ten years are generally clothed in citizens' dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include counts and cultural observations about dress adoption as an indicator of assimilation or progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for surveys, salaries, and reconstruction funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative recommendations: complete surveys as soon as possible, modify salaries of employes as previously stated, forward funds for reconstruction of saw-mill, and other practical administrative requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicit recommendations with justification (e.g., inability to build without saw-mill lumber), reference prior communications (letters of March 9, 1880), and include estimated costs where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency financial accounting and transfer procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Report of unexpended balance refunded to U.S. Treasury (e.g., $1,985.86), transfer of agency and government property to successor, and mailing of final accounts to the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include closing financial statements, amounts refunded, compliance with transfer instructions, and confirmation of account submission.
